question: What is our unified Pass 2 judgment on Cheniere Energy (LNG) as of November 20, 2026?

epigraph.quote: Own great physical infrastructure at a margin of safety; never mistake a geopolitical shipping spike for permanent earning power.
epigraph.author: Cheniere Pass 2 Re-Underwriting Desk

web_blocks.html: Cheniere Energy, Inc. (NYSE: LNG) runs America's largest LNG export platform (~56 mtpa across Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi) backed by $112.2 billion of revenue backlog [2][31]. Pass 1 blind-spot forensics confirm a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality rating and PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. CCL Stage 3 finished ahead of schedule in August 2026, yet 2026 results leaned on Strait of Hormuz marketing spikes while gross debt rose to $24.138 billion [3][31][35].

At Friday's November 20, 2026 close of $294.84, LNG holds a clean Stage 2 uptrend (+14.65% 63-day relative strength vs. SPY) [38][42]. Stripping out Hormuz windfalls cuts normalized 2027E EBITDA to $7.30 billion and net parent FCF to $3.20 billion (5.31% yield vs. 5.04% 10-year Treasury) [35][42]. Against a normalized Base target of $315.00 and an upward-ratcheted stop at $281.56, support asymmetry is 1.35:1 (<1.50:1 hurdle). Our dual verdict is New Capital: REJECTED (TIER_0) and Current Holding (6.2472 Schwab shares): HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP at $281.56.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed institutional underwriting monograph on Cheniere Energy, ticker LNG, updated through November 20, 2026. This Pass 2 edition pairs a price-blind audit of Cheniere's Q3 Form 10-Q and November Form 8-K filings with an unbiased re-computation of valuation, technicals, and portfolio risk.

Here is our conclusion up front. Cheniere remains America's premier 56-million-tonne-per-year LNG exporter with $112.2 billion in contracted backlog and strong Corpus Christi Stage 3 execution. Yet Pass 1 uncovered two forces narrowing the margin of safety: 2026 guidance leaned on temporary Strait of Hormuz spikes in short-term marketing, while gross debt rose to $24.14 billion ahead of $1.2 billion in 5.800% parent notes.

On normalized 2027 cash flows—$7.30 billion Adjusted EBITDA and $3.20 billion net parent free cash flow—LNG yields 5.31% versus 5.04% 10-year Treasuries. Our unbiased Base Case fair value is $315.00, offering 1.35-to-1 support asymmetry above our ratcheted $281.56 stop. We assign REJECTED (TIER_0) to new capital and HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP on our 6.2472 Schwab shares ($1,841.92, 2.45% weight) with the stop raised from $278.52 to $281.56.

book_callouts.title: BEFORE YOU READ
book_callouts.text: Keep new-capital discipline separate from existing-position management. At $294.84, Cheniere's Stage 2 chart still merits a tight trailing stop on held shares, even as normalized post-Hormuz valuation blocks fresh buying.
